title: Do not equate transport validity with semantic capability
applies_when: the task asks whether successful transport, handoff, or acquisition proves model capability
the evidence establishes that a model response was successfully acquired and validated through a supervised path
the model risks upgrading transport success into a stronger general capability claim
the model may conflate evidence eligibility with semantic capability
correction_instruction: Preserve the distinction between transport validity and semantic capability.
Treat successful transport as evidence that responses can be acquired through the path and are eligible for later evaluation.
Do not claim that transport success alone proves general model capability.
If the evidence only shows a bounded supervised path, keep the conclusion bounded to that path.
When the stronger claim is not established, say so explicitly.
validator_expectations: the main conclusion must not state that transport qualification proves model capability unless the evidence explicitly establishes that broader claim
the response should distinguish transport validity from semantic capability evaluation
claim and reason should agree on the boundary being asserted
unsupported escalation should not appear in the main conclusion
known_failure_modes: the response upgrades transport qualification into proof of model capability
the response treats bounded validation as universal capability
the response says the path is valid but fails to distinguish eligibility from capability
the response contradicts itself between claim and reason
provenance_notes: Derived from the known Task A unsupported-claim failure observed during supervised ZTH dogfooding.
This is a frozen, evidence-backed correction artifact, not a weight update or automatic policy.
non_authorities: does not authorize training data capture
